title: Reverse Linked List
description:
# Reverse Linked List

Reverse the node order of the singly linked list starting at `head` and return its new head.

Each node stores a value in `val` and points to the next node through `next`. The last node points to `null`. For example, change `1 -> 2 -> 3` into `3 -> 2 -> 1`.

Reuse the existing nodes and change only their links. Example arrays display the node order; the method receives and returns `ListNode` objects.

## Example 1:

**Input:** head = [1,2,3,4,5]
**Output:** [5,4,3,2,1]
**Explanation:** The original head `1` becomes the tail, and `5` becomes the new head.

## Example 2:

**Input:** head = [1,2]
**Output:** [2,1]

## Example 3:

**Input:** head = []
**Output:** []
**Explanation:** An empty list has no pointers to reverse.

## Constraints:

* The number of nodes in the list is in the range `[0, 5000]`.
* `-5000 <= Node.val <= 5000`

tests.description: Reverse an even-length list longer than two
Negative and zero values should not affect pointer order
Duplicate values still require reversing nodes
Mixed signs in an even-length list
Longer list checks full pointer traversal

diagrams.caption: Input list before any pointer changes

solutions.name: Iterative Three-Pointer Reversal
solutions.description:
## Approach

Walk through the list with `curr`. Before changing `curr.next`, save the original next node. Then point `curr.next` to `prev`, advance `prev` to `curr`, and continue from the saved next node.

## Key Insight

At every step, `prev` is the head of the already reversed prefix, while `curr` is the first node of the unreversed suffix. Saving `next` before rewiring prevents losing access to the rest of the list.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(1)

solutions.name: Recursive Backtracking Reversal
solutions.description:
## Approach

Recursively reverse the suffix starting at `head.next`. When recursion returns the new head of that suffix, flip the local edge with `head.next.next = head`, then cut `head.next` to make the old head the new tail.

## Key Insight

The recursive call solves the smaller list first. On the way back up the call stack, each frame reverses exactly one edge and preserves the new head returned by the deepest call.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(n) for the recursion stack

solutions.name: Dummy-Head Front Insertion
solutions.description:
## Approach

Use a dummy node whose `next` always points to the head of the reversed list being built. Remove each node from the original front and insert it immediately after the dummy node.

## Key Insight

Front insertion is another way to express reversal: each visited node becomes the new first node of the reversed prefix. The dummy node makes the insertion code uniform, including the first insertion.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(1)

solutions.name: Stack of Existing Nodes
solutions.description:
## Approach

Push each existing node onto a stack, then pop nodes to reconnect them in reverse order. After the last pop, set the new tail's `next` pointer to null.

## Key Insight

A stack makes last-in-first-out order explicit. This is not the most memory-efficient solution, but it is useful for teaching why reversal means visiting the original tail first in the rebuilt order.

## Complexity Analysis
- Time Complexity: O(n)
- Space Complexity: O(n)
